intro.heading: The cover is booked. The total is nowhere.
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: A night nurse goes off sick on a Tuesday, so the manager rings the agency. Over the next fortnight there is a second booking for a holiday gap and a third to cover a long term absence. Each call is sensible on its own. Each is agreed by phone, and the confirmation is an email in a busy inbox. At the end of the month the owner asks how much the home spent on agency cover, and the manager can only say it feels like a lot. Here is how that plays out.

trail.text: A night shift is short. The manager rings the agency.
Cover is found and the shift is safe.
Two more bookings follow, for a holiday gap and a long absence.
The owner asks what agency cover cost. The manager has a feeling, not a figure.
Booking emails, a diary note and three invoices that arrive later.
Nobody can say at a glance who from the agency is on site this week.
Whether the same people keep coming back, and which agency costs most.
“How much did agency cover cost us last quarter?” A rough guess is not an answer.

trail_close: Nothing here is a failure. The cover was needed and it worked. The gap is that the cost lives in scattered places. Here is how CareStream gives you one place to look.

talk.heading: The questions managers ask, and how CareStream answers them
talk.sub: Read this as a conversation. The questions are the ones we hear most.

items.q: What does CareStream actually show me about agency cover?
items.a: Once you add a booking, the Staff page shows a 12 month panel. It reports bookings, people, days and cost, with a breakdown by agency, and it shows who is active now.

items.q: Where do the figures come from?
items.a: From what you type in. When you add a booking you enter the agency, the first and last day and, if you wish, the day rate. Cost is the day rate times the days, counting both the first and the last day.

items.q: Does it read my agency invoices?
items.a: No. It does not import invoices or timesheets, so it will not match an invoice to the penny. It is a running view built from your own bookings. Your finance records stay the record of what you paid.

items.q: What if I do not know the day rate?
items.a: The rate is optional. If none was recorded, the cost for that booking shows as unknown and not as zero, so the total never quietly understates what you spent.

items.q: Will this reduce agency spend by itself?
items.a: No. It shows you the spend, which is the first step to deciding what to change. What you do with the picture, such as booking differently or building your own team, is your decision.

items.q: Do agency staff use up a place on our plan?
items.a: No. They are time boxed to the dates you set and do not use a seat on your plan. Their hub access ends 24 hours after the last day, and you get an email three days before.

items.q: Can agency staff do an induction in the hub?
items.a: Yes. They use the Staff Hub like your own staff, and you can enrol them in the induction flows you have marked as suitable for agency staff. A flow step is read a policy or answer a question. There is no manager signature step.

limits.heading: A running view of agency cover, not a finance system

cards.title: It does not read invoices or timesheets
cards.body: The spend is the day rate times the days you enter. It will differ from an invoice that includes extras, overtime or a different rate, so keep your accounts as the record of what you paid.

cards.title: It will not cut your bill by itself
cards.body: It makes the cost visible by month and by agency. Deciding to book differently, or to recruit, is a management decision and CareStream makes none of it.

cards.title: It does not check agency documents
cards.body: Checks such as identity and right to work stay with the agency. CareStream does not capture them, does not give agency staff supervisions or appraisals, and it is not a rota or payroll tool.

items.q: How do I track agency cover in a care service?
items.a: Add each booking on the Staff page with the agency name, first day, last day and day rate. The 12 month panel then totals bookings, people, days and cost, with a breakdown by agency.

items.q: What are agency staff costs based on in CareStream?
items.a: The day rate and dates you enter. The cost is the day rate times the days, counting the first and last day. They are not read from invoices or timesheets, so treat the figure as a running view.

items.q: What happens if I leave the day rate blank?
items.a: The cost for that booking shows as unknown, not zero. You can edit the booking later to add or change the day rate, extend the dates or rename the agency.

items.q: Can I reduce agency spend with CareStream?
items.a: CareStream does not reduce it for you. It shows how much cover you use, how many days and which agency, which helps you decide what to change. Many services also look at rota planning, and our guide to scheduling training around a rota covers that side.

items.q: Does an agency worker need an induction?
items.a: The CQC guidance on Regulation 18 says providers must have an induction programme that prepares staff for their role. Whatever your service decides, CareStream lets you give them induction steps to read and questions to answer, and keeps the record.

items.q: Do agency staff count towards our staff limit?
items.a: No. They do not use a seat on your plan. They are also left out of the compliance register, supervisions and appraisals, and staff incentives.

items.q: How is the number of staff on shift decided?
items.a: That is your judgement as the provider. Regulation 18 requires that sufficient numbers of suitably qualified, competent, skilled and experienced persons are deployed. CareStream does not decide your staffing levels or run a rota.

items.q: Is the spend panel the same as a budget report?
items.a: No. It is a view of your agency worker bookings from the figures you enter. It does not hold your budget, your invoices or your accounts.

guide.heading: A practical way to keep agency cover under control
guide.lede: Agency cover is sometimes the right answer. The aim is not to avoid it but to know what it costs, who you rely on and whether each person is ready for the shift.

sections.h3: Start with one list of bookings
paragraphs: Most services can tell you the agency they ring first, but not the number of days booked last quarter. Start by recording every booking in one place at the time it is made. Note the agency, the first and last day and the agreed day rate, and treat the confirmation email as the source.

Review the list monthly. Ask three questions. Which agency do we use most? Do the same people keep returning? Which bookings were long enough that a different arrangement might have suited the service better? Nothing here needs a spreadsheet to be perfect. It needs to be current.

The wording of Regulation 18 asks for sufficient numbers of suitably qualified, competent, skilled and experienced persons to be deployed. The CQC guidance expects a systematic approach to working out the number of staff and the skills needed. Agency cover is one way services meet that need, so it helps to see how much you lean on it.
checklist: Add each booking with the agency, dates and day rate on the day you make it.
Check the spend panel once a month and compare it with your own accounts.
Look at the breakdown by agency and note any you rely on more than you planned.
Make sure each person has read your key policies before or on their first shift.

guide.note: For the owner or the board. Keep the spend view, your accounts and your staffing decisions together, so you can explain why cover was booked and what it cost.
